heard: Astronauts spotted a giant eye staring back from the Sahara. Gemini crews used the 25-mile circular rings as a navigation landmark. Scientists first thought a giant meteor smashed the African desert, but geological surveys found zero evidence of a cosmic impact. Instead, underground magma pushed Earth's crust upward into a dome. Wind and water carved away softer rock over millions of years, leaving high, concentric ridges of hard rock behind. Fringe theories claimed the matching rings were Plato's lost Atlantis, but no ancient city ever built what astronauts saw from space.
